rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.figure: Fed Dec quarter-point hike ~97% (CME FedWatch via Hercules); ECB Dec ~93%; BoE Dec ~82%; BoJ Dec ~85%; BoC Dec ~80%; RBA Dec hold ~99%
rows.read: A December Fed hike is all but certain, which keeps the dollar firm. The European Central Bank, Bank of England, Bank of Japan and Bank of Canada are all still expected to hike in December, though soft French and Spanish inflation weakens the case for more European hikes after that.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: China industrial profits Oct +20.1% y/y; US goods trade gap Oct −$149.5B (fcst −$135.9B); Germany unemployment +9K (fcst +5K); Canada Q3 GDP fcst ~1.3%–1.5% annualized (Mon Nov 30)
rows.read: Chinese factory profits grew strongly, good news for Australia. The US goods trade gap widened sharply as imports of artificial intelligence equipment surged, a drag on US growth this quarter. Germany's labour market softened, and Canada's growth figures on Monday are expected to show a sharp slowdown.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: France CPI Nov 2.9% y/y (fcst 3.2%); Spain CPI Nov 4.1% (fcst 4.7%), core 2.6%; Tokyo core CPI Nov 2.9% (fcst 3.0%); Australia CPI Oct 4.9%
rows.read: Inflation cooled far more than expected in France and Spain as fuel got cheaper, which weighed on the euro. US and Australian inflation still run hot, keeping their central banks leaning toward higher rates.

rows.figure: Gold ~$3,652, +3.3% on the week; USD/CHF −0.4% and USD/JPY +0.6% on the week; US 10-year ~4.92%
rows.read: A slide in technology shares midweek briefly sent money into the yen and franc, then stocks recovered. Gulf attacks on ships kept worry high, and that worry went into gold rather than currencies.

rows.figure: Brent January settled $95.44, about +3% on the week; Brent February ~$92.57; WTI $83.08; gold ~$3,652

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: Hedge funds (CFTC, Nov 17): USD index −1.3K (flipped short), EUR −76.6K, GBP +28.8K, JPY −23.8K, CHF −19.8K, CAD −72.1K, AUD +38.0K, NZD −23.6K; asset managers GBP −104.6K, AUD −182.7K, EUR +147.2K
rows.read: The latest weekly figures show hedge funds have turned slightly against the dollar, while still betting against the euro, the kiwi, the franc and, most strongly, the Canadian dollar. They still bet on the pound and the Aussie, where big long-term investors take the opposite side. Heavy bets against the loonie leave room for a fast unwind if Canadian hike bets keep growing.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: S&P France A+, outlook negative (Nov 27); France Q3 deficit 5.6% of GDP (INSEE via Hercules); NZ coalition 65 of 130 seats, 66 needed
rows.read: S&P kept France's credit rating but cut its outlook to negative, so all three big agencies now see a possible downgrade, a weight on the euro. New Zealand's government is one seat short of a majority, which adds doubt over its spending.
